original.target_description: Unassigned original side; not inspected in this source-grouped completion.

replication.target_description: Crowd-size photo selection: unresolved correspondence between H1 (Republicans versus Democrats) and H8 (Trump versus Clinton voters). Both ask which photo has more people; they are distinct samples/tests.

n.sample_role: Candidate analytic participants: 954 for H1 or 636 for H8; no single target assigned.
n.exclusions: Prior to analysis: survey duration below 5 or above 60 minutes, age below 18 or above 100, duplicate IP of earlier completer, non-USA IP. Final sample 954 of 1018 complete respondents (1114 partial-or-complete respondents). H8 additionally includes Trump and Clinton voters only, excluding other candidates, nonvoters and cannot-remember respondents.

notes: Identity verified from the supplied text title, Robert M. Ross and Neil Levy byline, Collabra: Psychology Vol. 9 Issue 1 (2023), and DOI 10.1525/collabra.68054. This is the primary extended-replication report, with Methods, Results, Discussion and references, not an abstract-only excerpt or preregistration. No PDF was supplied; no render or acquisition attempted. Two candidate critical tests: H1, p. 4, Republican versus Democrat crowd-size accuracy, printed χ2(1) = 5.365, p = .021; H8, p. 5, Trump versus Clinton voter crowd-size accuracy, printed χ2(1) = 4.569, p = .033. Candidate analytic participant sums from explicitly mutually exclusive final groups: H1 532 + 422 = 954; H8 303 + 333 = 636. These are candidate sums only, not assigned n values. The neutral description combines voting and partisan group labels. The p. 4 locator favors H1 but does not independently resolve the description’s alternative voting-based comparison; no mapping by input order or numeric agreement was made. Prior to analysis: survey duration below 5 or above 60 minutes, age below 18 or above 100, duplicate IP of earlier completer, non-USA IP. Final sample 954 of 1018 complete respondents (1114 partial-or-complete respondents). H8 additionally includes Trump and Clinton voters only, excluding other candidates, nonvoters and cannot-remember respondents. Reported success is the authors’ explicit central-replication verdict; both candidate comparisons are described as statistically significant. It does not resolve row-specific test correspondence. Unassigned fields are null placeholders and were not re-extracted.
